Dylan / team —

Thanks — high level guidance below (state rules simplified):

- Texas (TX): Strong preference for a resale cert that lists the specific seller legal entity or a notarized affidavit tying the marketplace relationship to the named seller. Blanket certificates that only list the marketplace operator are commonly rejected.
- Washington (WA) & California (CA): Generally accept a marketplace-wide cert if accompanied by a signed seller onboarding attestation that ties the seller ID to the cert.
- New York (NY): Accepts blanket certificates in many cases but we should confirm presence of the seller tax ID (EIN) on the invoice.

Operationally: we need a CSV mapping (seller_id, legal_entity_name, tax_id, invoice_ref). For TX sellers, a notarized copy is preferable; otherwise finance may keep invoice on hold.

If Acme can provide a signed attestation that: (a) lists the seller IDs and legal entity names, and (b) confirms that Acme Marketplace is authorized to accept resale certificates on behalf of those sellers, that will speed verification. The attestation can be a short PDF; notarization only required for TX and a couple of small municipalities.

I’ve attached an internal checklist we use to clear holds (not included in external email). Happy to review the submitted docs once you upload them.

- Marcus
Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference
